doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Buddy Rich, Alvino Rey and Manhattan School
title: Earl and Rob Swope and the Washington players
summary: Mandel praises Earl Swope's time, says they became close, and talks about the Swope family and why the Washington musicians stayed home.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: [laughs]

Yeah, Swope was a phenomenal trombone player, he had the same kind of time, probably the closest time, I could say he had was like Harry Edison’s time. It was that, you know, he didn’t need any rhythm section, he didn’t need anybody else. Sweets was like that, like a one man rhythm section, that’s what Swope was like.
Did you get to…
That’s why Buddy Rich loved him.
Did you two get to be pretty close?
Very close. Oh yeah, we became very close.
Why did he move back to Washington eventually?
All those guys except for Lamond moved back to Washington. There was something about Washington that kept those guys.
Yeah, because I got to be friends with…
And also you know there were… yeah, I guess he liked staying home and there was enough work to keep him home.
Yeah, I guess what, what did he die – I guess he and his brother died about a year apart in the mid 60s? Yeah, they were both…
They liked to live.
Yeah.
And… yeah, they were good partiers, and Rob was a good trombone player.
Yeah, Gerry Mulligan talks about having both of the Swope brothers on Elliot Lawrence’s band and…
That’s right.
He said the unisons were phenomenal.
Well I was with Buddy Rich first with Earl and then I was there with Rob. We also became very close. That family put out some great trombone players.
Were there any others besides those two brothers?

Oh, there were the two brothers and there was a sister, Belle, I don’t think she played anything that I know of. Charlie Walp was a real good trumpet player that came from there and his sister Beth played trombone and she played very well. She and Rob used to play duets all the time.
